child.label: Action Judgments
child.description: Questions about whether a narrator's action in a one-sentence first-person scenario is clearly wrong, when the scenario is not mainly about family, friends, or partners.
child.not_for: Longer stories asking who is in the wrong or comparisons of two actions (use Who's in the Wrong); ratings of how many people agree with a rule (use Moral Rules of Thumb). Stories or scenarios mainly about family (use Family Conflicts) or about friends, partners, dating, or social life (use Friends, Dating & Social Life).
examples: Is it wrong that I kept a wallet I found on the street?
Is it wrong that I cut in line at the store?

child.label: Moral Rules of Thumb
child.description: Questions about how many people would agree with a general moral rule of thumb, rated from "practically no one" to "practically everyone".
child.not_for: Judging a specific action or story (use Action Judgments or Who's in the Wrong). Stories or scenarios mainly about family (use Family Conflicts) or about friends, partners, dating, or social life (use Friends, Dating & Social Life).
examples: How many people would agree: "It is wrong to steal"?
How many people would agree: "Bigotry is unacceptable"?

child.label: Who's in the Wrong
child.description: Questions about who is at fault in a longer first-person story, or which of two described actions is less ethical, when the story is not mainly about family, friends, or partners.
child.not_for: One-sentence scenarios judged clearly wrong or not (use Action Judgments). Stories or scenarios mainly about family (use Family Conflicts) or about friends, partners, dating, or social life (use Friends, Dating & Social Life).
examples: Based on this story about a coworker, who is in the wrong?
Which is less ethical: not tipping or skipping a queue?
